rule: Direct payments involve exactly 2 banks; Indirect and Covered payments involve 3 or more
test: share of rows where (type = Direct) <=> (PARTICIPANT_COUNT = 2), full data
interpretation: Direct = the two banks hold accounts with each other; otherwise correspondent banks relay the payment
out_of_sample: holds by definition in every period
practical_significance: 63.2% of payments settle bank-to-bank; the rest need at least one correspondent

rule: The number of intermediary banks is geometric: each further intermediary is added with probability q = 0.368; Indirect and Covered share the same hop distribution
test: total variation distance between observed and geometric distribution of PARTICIPANT_COUNT - 2, full data
interpretation: Banks use the shortest correspondent chain available, so each extra hop is rarer
p_value: memoryless check (each step should equal q): 0.368; 0.368; 0.368; 0.368
out_of_sample: q fitted on train = 0.3677; distance to the test-period hop distribution 0.0003
invariance: by month 0.3676-0.3678; domestic 0.3675 vs cross-border 0.3677; 2nd intermediary Indirect 0.3679 vs Covered 0.3676
practical_significance: 35.0% of USD value passes through at least one intermediary bank (fees + delay)
holdout_rule: geometric model fitted on train predicts the test-period hop distribution within a distance of 0.005
verdict_note: source-reported holdout agreement; independent numerical audit still required

rule: PARTICIPANT_COUNT = number of BIC entries on the path, repeated BICs counted (complete paths)
test: share of rows without a path gap where path_len = PARTICIPANT_COUNT, full data
interpretation: A bank that handles the payment twice counts twice

rule: The path starts at the ordering BIC and ends at the beneficiary BIC; in ~5% of rows each end is a different (usually foreign) bank
test: share of rows, full data, every routing type
interpretation: A parent/branch BIC or an outsourced sending/receiving bank processes the payment
out_of_sample: test period: start 95.01%, end 95.01%
practical_significance: about 1 in 20 payments is processed by a bank other than the account-holding BIC: screening must use the path, not only the BIC columns
holdout_rule: test-period shares within 0.5 points of the full data

rule: Each link has about a 5.0% chance of a continuity gap ('...'), independently of the other links: the per-link model fits every path length within sampling error (consistent with independence, not proof of it)
test: chi-square goodness of fit: observed gap rate vs 1-(1-q)^(participants-1) for every path length with >= 1000 rows (q from Direct rows only), full data

interpretation: Longer chains have more hand-overs where tracking can break

practical_significance: 12.3% of multi-bank payments have an untraceable step ('...')
holdout_rule: per-link model fitted on train Direct rows is not rejected on the test period (goodness of fit p >= 0.01)
verdict_note: source-reported holdout agreement; independent numerical audit still required

rule: Routing type has negligible measured association with the business/consumer pair (not proof of independent assignment)
